body:

First I got about 1000 word email saying they were sorry I was leaving and to always contact support in the first instance - which is what I did! Then when I emailed again I got the “this is a known issue” response. It feels as though they’ve contracted out to a robot, I’ve lost faith in my ability to actually raise a question and get it sorted. I still think the apps great and hope that I’ll remain subscribed (once only) but I wish they’d train their customer support robots to answer questions.

title: Could be brilliant app but fundamentally flawed.
body:
Bad flaws. Poor customer service. And they haven’t addressed things people have raised here over 4 years ago. Too expensive for an app they don’t update or listen to users about. 

This would easily be a five star because when I first got this app I wowed so much as I went through the features and aesthetics that I thought it was perfect. But it’s missing a few things that mean I’m not going to subscribe. 1: I wanted to move other apps data here. I’ve been not drinking for 70 days and I wanted to add that streak but you can’t go back and add data to past days. Also if I accidentally miss a day or press something wrong and only see it the next day, I can’t add it. Essentially chains can easily be destroyed by little mistakes and all that motivation and effort in recording it lost. 2: I wanted to use the fast timer which lasts 22 hours for me. But it’s sooo silly that you can’t record two timers at once. And if I close the app totally the timer goes and a missed fast is recorded. If I want to continue my reading timer the fast timer goes off. Meaning the timer there is useless taking away my initial joy at how seamlessly designed this app is. 3: it does silly things like sometimes saying I skipped a day when I haven’t and this is demotivating. It also shouldn’t say a day has been skipped when your aim is 4/7 days a week for something. Maybe say that at the end of the week but not when you don’t intend to do it every day on the first place. 4: you can undo something which is great but only sometimes. It seems properly closing the app and reopening it makes it impossible to press undo. I had to remake new goals a few times in the first day to clear a skipped task I didn’t skip or something that was wrong. And when I changed things it said all history will be wiped. Meaning in future when it messes up I will lose all history and all that pride at my effort and the data I want to collect essentially for tracking my mental and physical health. So yeah lots of potential but I won’t be paying for this app yet. I’ll look for something cheaper or free that works better still.

title: It’s good but a few things I would change
body: I like this app. The interface is more visual and a lot cleaner and less cluttered than other similar apps. I have ADHD so this is helpful to me. There is one thing I can’t do in Productive that I would like to be able to do. I wish there was like a general task list area where I could dump all the tasks that are in my head but without setting a day or time on them yet. Like I know I need to create a dedicated area in my house for stretching but I don’t want to commit to doing that today for example or on a specific date. I just want it in a general list so I can free up space in my head but just have it in a general area until I’m ready to schedule it. I also wish I could create my own challenges rather than having to pick ones others are doing. With the challenges I also wish you could see what they actually entail before committing to them. Like with the bed time routine challenge - it turns out it’s just getting your clothes ready the night before. I don’t need that challenge as I wear the same thing every day. But I only found out that’s what the challenge entailed after I signed up. It’s easy enough to delete the challenge but that’s after I’ve wasted minutes signing up to it. Thats the opposite of productive. Other than that I really like the app. I wish it was more brightly coloured as I think it would help encourage me to access the app more (but that’s the dopamine junkie talking probably).

body:

⚠️ this app is NOT integrated between your iPhone & iPad. ⚠️
Sure you can download the app on your iPhone & iPad (as advertised), but they are “2 separate apps”. 
Why the developer has chosen to mislead us before handing over our cash, and have the only app in the store that is absolutely useless being effectively a separate app on each device, is frankly ‘Bizarre’, and just lazy to not add that extra line of code, which really is that straightforward.

The potential is here to make something that is ‘great’, “Amazing”! But, it’s more about that feeling, that they have my hard earned money now, and I feel VERY disrespected. 

As a small business owner, I always think twice before leaving a negative review, and try give the benefit of doubt. But I am annoyed, & you would be too, if I didn’t inform you properly.

title: Needs Work!
body:
Used to be a great app - but it got lost. 

The developers are too focused on the animation/graphics and making it look pretty than addressing the core functionality of how the app improves people’s lives or listening to their users. 

It’s not agile enough to reinforce creating good habits and can dishearten your progress entirely. Why should you loose your 300 day streak of Yoga and start from 0 if you forgot to take your Vitamins one day? 🤨 

There is a plethora of user reviews asking for the same functionality to be addressed and I myself have emailed the developers twice in the last 2 years. 

What did we get instead?...A new Christmas update where the background has Christmas Trees 🙄👍

The “Widget” continues the trend - a tiny single number of habits - with three quarters of the widget displaying a graphic of a hill and tree? 🤨 Surely that space could be utilized for analytics a little more...I don’t know...Productive!?

Finally - both the watch & phone app need to be streamlined, completing a habit should take 1 tap - not 4 swipes & 2 taps. 

After 2 years of waiting for it to redeem itself - I finally jumped ship to the Streaks app and wow! It’s so much better. Simple, intuitive, slick, agile, great app for watch & phone, the widget is productive and beautiful and it talks to Apple health so I don’t need to tap anything at all. It’s what I hoped this app could be. All for a small one off fee instead of a subscription model. 

I’m very sorry guys - I hate to give negative criticism. But I have to say and tell it how it is 🤷‍♂️

title: Update is terrible
body:
Ever since I started with this app, in Jan 2018, the stats don’t work. When you delete or reset a habit, it removes your perfect day from the day you started the habit. But that’s not a huge issue for me.
I’ve had problems since then with the app crashing after some updates. But it’s a useful app and the crashing was fixed so I kept using it.
The new update to version 2.0.0 is dreadful. I opened it this morning. Rather than having morning, afternoon, evening and all day tasks in one list like before, I now have to scroll sideways from morning list to all day. And since it is the morning, it opens the app to the morning list, not the all day list, even though the morning list is empty (I set all my habits to be all day). The list of habits is now a smaller part of my screen so I can’t see as many on the screen at once. It also decided that all the weekly tasks for this week hadn’t been done, even though I did them on Monday (writing this on Saturday) and that I needed all my weekly tasks to have notifications (previously weekly tasks didn’t show notifications until sunday when it is my last day to do them). The update is frustrating to the point that I erased my entire phone so I could restore to a backup with the old version of this app. I’m either never updating this app again or I’m finding a different productivity app. Yes the update looks nice, but the thing that attracted me to this app over other to-do list apps was that it was simple. Complicated lists distract from being productive. And the update has just complicated things.
Two stars instead of one because the pre-update version is pretty good and useful.

I found a hack around it by using Siri shortcuts to trigger the habit which then adds it to the counter, but seems very weird you can’t do this manually. 

Also if you change any of the goals the stats will totally disappear. Going by what I said above I’d like to start with my goal of yoga once a week, start small. Once I’ve mastered that I want to increase it to twice a week. Now all the stats are totally reset, which is silly as you’re only increasing the target. I can’t imagine this use case is that weird? I would find setting a higher target and failing every week demotivating.

I love the interface and general feel of the app, I think it just needs to have some more comprehensive customisation. I understand that simplicity is a selling point, but there could be some advanced options for power users. 

Would love to know if these features are on your roadmap, I’ve gone back to a good old fashioned paper chart which works for me.

title: I do like this app
body:
It’s easy to use, easy to understand. However, it is far from perfect: 

* The “free” version needs to allow more than 3 habits. How can you accurately gauge if you like the app when you can only list 3 items?
* You should be able to set days for your habits. At the moment, even with premium, I can’t see a way of setting a specific habit for a specific day, only a time of day. Which is no use. Being able to set habits further in advance would be good, like dentist appointments. 
* Daily and weekly to do lists would also be very helpful and would make the app more competitive against apps such as Habitica. 
* It should be easy to see what habits you currently have listed. I had several listed multiple times and I can’t work out how to see what habits I’ve already got. 
* It’s expensive! £20 a year?? Once the trial is over I’ll most likely be cancelling due to the above. Why would I pay a yearly subscription when I can get the same somewhere else for free or cheaper? Either a £20 one off price or a MUCH lower yearly cost would be better
* I’ve tried it several times over the last couple of years and there just doesn’t seem to be any changes. Almost like the developers aren’t really changing or improving anything or listening to what their customers are saying and for £20 a year, I’d want to see a LOT of upgrades and changes.

title: Updating to Premium
body:
There’s a lot that this app does do: it’s immaculate, easy to use & an absolutely great concept.  I struggle with making myself keep ontop of routine because in my job, it’s constantly changing.

However - I would recommend allowing a few more habits to be created without updating to premium. There’s no way I can try the app out properly with only three habits. I need more than that to get through the week! & because the ‘subscription continues until cancelled’ I do not trust myself to take a free trial - those of us with busy enough lives to warrant having a to-do app probably don’t remember trivial things like cancelling an app subscription! I might consider allowing a few more habits to be made on the free version OR setting up a cancellation feature. 

Also, this app would be absolutely fantastic if you had a simple to-do list feature also - somewhere to write one-off tasks as well as keep on top of things you repeat regularly.  Just something to consider (would be absolutely unparalleled if this existed).

I liked the app but found it a bit disorganised: if I didn't tick off the workout I did in the morning until the afternoon, then it wouldn't have priority again until the next afternoon. With 'Productive' you start by grouping your tasks into 'morning', 'afternoon' or 'evening' and they always show up at the right time, no matter what time you mark them as complete. body: A very well-made little app, and I appreciate the fact that the free version allows you to properly try out the app by tracking five habits before buying. How about an element of gamification to encourage habit-building? Even just a message saying "Congrats, a perfect day!", with increasingly enthusiastic messages if you string together a few perfect days in a row! (Yes, I know that's what tags and categories are for, but sorting them every day??) 

I like a short and manageable task list. Moving all the daily stuff to a separate app just made sense for me. This app gets around the clutter in an excellent manner. This means that nothing daily and mundane is missed and my main tasks app reminds me of ongoing projects, business and non-recurrent stuff.

If you have a lot of recurring tasks, or are trying to change your habitual patterns then look no further than this app. Brilliant!

body:

Things such as mindful thinking, stretching, getting to sleep by 11pm, drinking more water, reading, working out, have all been made attainable by simply having this very neat schedule, complete at your own pace with no set time! I think its great as not actually setting a specific time and just a 'morning' 'afternoon' or 'evening' time gives you the flexibility and freedom to get it done without it feeling like a task. It makes habits seemingly ease into your life.
I would seriously recommend spending the extra £2.99 to upgrade as I did, even though I never spend cash in the app store aha. 
I hope this review convinces someone else to download because the app really does work in this surprising way :)
